name: Antiquities on the Loose

abilities.text: Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. Then if ~ was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control.

notes: 'cast from anywhere other than your hand' is the ELSE branch of the cast-from-hand condition - an exact negation, not an approximation: the then branch is deliberately empty. The counters go on each Spirit you control (the two new tokens included) through for-each.

issues: Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. — expected Two 2/2 red-and-white Spirit creature tokens named 'Spirit'. — scripted token count 2, 2/2, colors ['R','W'], types ['Creature'], subtypes ['Spirit'] — correct. No `name` given, so the engine names them 'Spirit token' (game.ts:1332) rather than 'Spirit'; purely cosmetic. The two scenario failures are NOT a script defect: tokens are built with makeObject(..., src.def, ...), so their def.name is 'Antiquities on the Loose', and the harness's findByName (scenarioDsl.ts:418) matches on def.name and scans the battlefield before the graveyard/exile, hitting the token instead of the sorcery. A script-side token name would not change def.name, so this is a harness limitation. — CR CR 111.4

Then if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control. — expected Exact negation of 'cast from your hand' — true for a flashback cast from the graveyard, false for a hand cast; counters go on every Spirit permanent you control, the two new tokens included. — scripted conditional {cast-from-hand} with an empty `then` and the work in `else`. characteristics.ts:432 reads (src.castWith?.from ?? 'hand') === 'hand' and game.ts:621 records the real cast zone, so a flashback cast from the graveyard takes the else branch. for-each over {subtypes:['Spirit'], who:'you'} defaults to the battlefield zone (refs.ts:142) and runs after the token op, so the new tokens are included. Correct.

Flashback {4}{W}{W} — expected Castable from the graveyard for {4}{W}{W}, then exiled. — scripted altCosts entry id 'flashback', cost {4}{W}{W}, from:'graveyard', exileAfter:true, and an explicit covers entry claiming the line. Correct; the flashback scenario's graveyardCount[0,0] and battlefield count both passed.

Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. — expected the two objects are named 'Spirit' — scripted token op omits `name`; tokens are built from the source card's def, so the scenario harness's findByName (scenarioDsl.ts:418, x.def.name) sees 'Antiquities on the Loose' on the battlefield — the cause of both scenario failures. Body, colors and count are right; a harness/naming artifact, not a rules error. — CR 111.4

Then if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control. — expected exact negation of 'cast from your hand'; a spell that was not cast at all (a copy) gets no counters; the new tokens are included — scripted correct — conditional {kind:'cast-from-hand'} with empty then and the counters in else; characteristics.ts:432 defaults castWith?.from to 'hand', so an uncast copy takes the then branch (no counters), matching the card. for-each over {subtypes:['Spirit'], who:'you'} covers the two fresh tokens plus pre-existing Spirits; the flashback scenario shows the pre-existing Spirit at 2/2 with one counter. — CR 702.34a / 608.2

Flashback {4}{W}{W} — expected castable from the graveyard for {4}{W}{W}, then exiled — scripted correct — altCosts flashback from:'graveyard', exileAfter:true, and a valid covers entry {line:'Flashback {4}{W}{W}', by:'altCosts'}; the exile-instead scenario passes — CR 702.34a
